key_headlines.title: Pohang AI Data Center Construction Accelerates with 600 Billion Won Investment
key_headlines.summary: The government is streamlining procedures for a 600 billion won AI data center in Pohang, Gyeongbuk, targeting operations by January 2028. The project is expected to generate 1.2 trillion won in production and create 4,000 jobs.

key_headlines.title: Consumer Loan Rates Surge to 6.33% Amid Economic Growth and Household Hardship
key_headlines.summary: Despite GDP growth exceeding expectations in Q3 2026, consumer loan rates jumped from 5.41% to 6.33%, hitting households hard with mortgage and jeonse rates rising 0.7% and 0.57% respectively. Small business default rates increased 0.1% in a month amid widespread business closures.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Apartment Jeonse Prices Reach All-Time High of 728.98 Million Won
key_headlines.summary: Seoul apartment jeonse prices hit record highs for the 39th consecutive month at 728.98 million won, with northern Seoul breaking the 600 million won mark for the first time. The gap between Seoul and national prices widened to 390 million won.

key_headlines.title: Audit Office Reveals Government Revenue Forecasting Errors Cost 51.5 Trillion Won Over Four Years
key_headlines.summary: The Board of Audit and Inspection found that the former Ministry of Strategy and Finance made systematic errors in corporate tax forecasting by applying outdated average statistics despite volatile external economic conditions, causing massive 50 trillion won revenue discrepancies over four years.

key_headlines.title: Performance Polarization Drives Layoffs in Construction and Battery Industries Despite Semiconductor Boom
key_headlines.summary: While Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix post record profits driving massive shareholder returns, other sectors like construction and battery industries are implementing restructuring and voluntary retirements. The K-shaped economic divide is now visible in employment patterns.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy is experiencing a paradoxical situation where headline GDP growth of 1.0% quarter-over-quarter contrasts sharply with consumer hardship. Despite semiconductor and technology sector booming, with Samsung and SK Hynix posting record earnings, domestic consumption remains weak with rising unemployment fears. The surge in consumer loan rates to 6.33% and increased small business default rates underscore the disconnect between macro growth and household financial stress, leading to widespread business closures.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The government faces significant fiscal challenges, with the Board of Audit and Inspection uncovering 50-51.5 trillion won in revenue forecasting errors over four years attributable to outdated estimation models rather than cyclical economic factors. The Bank of Korea warns that accelerated carbon neutrality policies could reduce annual growth rates by up to 0.07 percentage points by 2060. Additionally, next year's tax expenditures are projected to exceed 100 trillion won for the first time, with corporate benefits accounting for half of all tax breaks.
sections.Financial Markets: Seoul's KOSPI index surged 374.1 points (6.63%) closing at 6,012.44, reclaiming the 6,000 level ahead of the Fed's FOMC decision. The won-dollar exchange rate rose to 1,337.7 won. Institutional investors purchased over 4 trillion won in stocks this month, though asset management companies showed net selling of 700 billion won. US markets gained ahead of the expected Fed rate hold, with semiconductor stocks showing particular strength following strong earnings reports from SK Hynix.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's industrial landscape is becoming increasingly polarized, with semiconductor and battery sectors advancing rapidly while construction and traditional manufacturing face headwinds. Gumi City is emerging as a secondary batteries hub with investment in Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) centers and recycling infrastructure. Meanwhile, China is targeting dominance in AI large language models, humanoid robots, and semiconductors by 2030, intensifying global technology competition.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment jeonse prices have reached unprecedented levels at 728.98 million won with 39 consecutive months of increases, while northern Seoul districts broke the 600 million won barrier for the first time. Housing supply is expected to decline sharply, dropping from 25,452 units in 2026 to just 5,289 units by 2030, concentrating demand in Seoul where 63.9% of applicants from 94 metropolitan developments filed subscription requests.
sections.International Economy: The won-dollar exchange rate climbed 14 won ahead of the Fed's FOMC meeting, with markets expecting rate maintenance at 93.4% probability while Korean interest rate hikes remain likely. International crude oil prices remain elevated, supporting import prices and narrowing the Korea-US rate differential. China's real estate market shows signs of stress, prompting European banks to pull back lending while presenting opportunities for alternative credit markets.
sections.AI & Economy: The government is prioritizing AI infrastructure development, fast-tracking the Pohang AI data center project worth 600 billion won for January 2028 operations. South Korea's National Pension Service is considering venture capital investments in Silicon Valley to identify AI growth companies. However, domestic private equity funds are hesitant to invest in AI data centers due to large conglomerate designation risks, potentially ceding opportunities to foreign investors.
sections.Others: The government is strengthening coordination between science-technology and economic-industry policies through seven major SEED projects focusing on nuclear fusion, renewable energy, and advanced biotechnology. China faces severe youth unemployment with 4 million applicants competing for civil service positions at 97-to-1 average ratios as AI job displacement concerns grow. Japan and Germany are establishing AI high-level dialogue and pursuing defense technology cooperation, reflecting global geopolitical realignment.
